question.prompt: Solve the system \(\begin{cases}x+2y=8\\3x-y=3\end{cases}\). (Write the values of \(x\) and \(y\), in that order, separated by a comma.)

solutions.explanation: From the first equation, \(x=8-2y\). Substitute into the second equation: \(3(8-2y)-y=3\), \(24-7y=3\), \(y=3\), \(x=2\).
solutions.title: Isolate x and substitute

solutions.explanation:
The \(y\)-coefficients are \(2\) and \(-1\), so doubling the second equation makes them opposite. Adding the doubled equation to the first eliminates \(y\):
\[
(x+2y)+2(3x-y)=8+2\cdot3,
\qquad 7x=14.
\]
Thus \(x=2\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(2+2y=8\), so \(y=3\). Therefore, the answer in the requested order is \(2,3\).
solutions.title: Double and add to eliminate y
